newsitem.title: LEBANON: Arrest warrant issued for Lebanese in Red Army case.
newsitem.headline: Arrest warrant issued for Lebanese in Red Army case.

text.p: A Beirut judge issued an arrest warrant on Friday against a Lebanese woman on charges of helping five alleged Japanese Red Army guerrillas commit offences against Lebanese law.
Investigative Judge Saeed Mirza issued the warrant against acupuncturist Omayah Abboud, detained along with five other Japanese nationals since February 15.

At least 50 Lebanese lawyers volunteered on Friday to defend the five Japanese suspects identified by Lebanon's Prosecutor General Adnan Addoum as Kozo Okamoto, Masao Adachi, Mariko Yamamoto, Kazuo Tohira and Haruo Wako. Japan says these are the names of Japanese Red Army guerrillas.
A spokesman for the lawyers said the decision was an act of loyalty towards the guerrillas who had stood by Arabs in their struggle against Israel.

"Our decision to defend Kozo (Okamoto) and his comrades is an act of faithfulness and a return of favour because they stood by us in the past, in our just nationalistic struggle," Hani Sleiman told Reuters.

All five suspects are on the international wanted list on charges arising from activities of the Japanese Red Army, which in the 1970s staged a string of attacks including plane hijackings and hostage-takings and linked up with the Palestinians in their fight against Israel.
The lawyers union later appointed two other lawyers, Farouq Yaghi and Nohad Jabr, to act for the defence at pre-trial investigations due to begin on Saturday, judicial sources said.
This was a temporary measure while the suspects make their own decisions on choosing their lawyers.
Sleiman, who is also Abboud's lawyer, told Reuters that she denied the charges. She told the judge that Adachi was one of her patients and that she never knew his real identity.
Abboud sometimes visited Adachi at his home where she met Yamamoto, Tohira and Wako. She never met Okamoto before, the judge said.

Okamoto, 49, took part in a 1972 shootout at Tel Aviv's Lod airport in which 24 people died and 78 were injured. He was sentenced to life imprisonment in Israel but was released in a Palestinian-Israeli prisoner swap in 1985.

Beirut Prosecutor Abdallah Bitar charged them on Thursday with possessing and using forged passports, forging Lebanese government official stamps, entering the country illegally and illegal residence.
Addoum said then the charges carried penalties of up to seven years hard labour but lawyers told Reuters on Friday the penalties ranged from five to 10 years.
The investigative judge will either order the suspects to stand trial or release them after completing his investigation.
Three other Japanese detainees were released on Thursday.
